questionText:
A person travelled a distance of 150 km and then returned to the starting point.
The time taken for the outward journey was 2&1/2 hours more than that for the return journey. His speed for the return journey was 10 km/h more than that for the outward journey. His speed for the return journey, in km/h, was:
solutionText: dist =( s1 - s2 / s1 * S2  )     * TIME DIFF

questionText: Ashok runs 2&2/3 times as fast as Bharat. If Ashok gives Bharat a head start of 160 m, then how far must the winning post be so that Ashok and Bharat can reach it at the same time?

One-third of a journey is covered at a speed of 62 km/hr, the next one-third of the journey is covered at a speed of 99 km/hr, and the remaining one-third is covered at a speed of 51 km/hr. What is the average speed for the entire journey, rounded off to 1 decimal place?
